messages:
tara: heads-up — ran a short canary this morning for v2-model on /generate, saw a small spike in p95 latency in us-west-2. Not critical but it breached our canary guard. Thinking we should try an automatic swapback flow that is more nuanced than just instant rollback. any thoughts?

liam: saw the same. p95 went from ~210ms -> ~420ms for a 10% canary over ~4m. no errors but increased tail. Do we want: 1) immediate swapback on threshold, 2) wait window + recheck, or 3) gradual shift back?

maya: +1 for wait window. we get false positives a lot during short blips. propose: threshold breach triggers a 3-min observation window, if still >threshold then swapback 100% to previous model. also surface the reason in console (latency/p95) and metric link.

sam: question: if west capacity is overloaded but global is fine, should we fallback regionally first (move canary traffic in region-> previous model) rather than full global swapback? might be less disruptive.

liam: agree. priority order proposal: regional capacity issues -> regional swapback; model-variant perf regression -> variant swapback; global infra capacity -> fallback to lower-cost variant or lower-reqs (quantized) + notify.

maya: +1 to priority list. also suggest making the swapback deploy action non-destructive: keep canary instance alive for quick re-validation, tag the rollout as "paused-swapback" so we can A/B debug.

deploy-bot: env=prod run=canary id=canary-2026-03-14-91 status=breach metric=p95 latency_us-west-2=420ms threshold=350ms

tara: ops question: how do we detect capacity vs model issue? we could correlate queue length, GPU util, and infra-errors. if util>85% -> capacity; if util normal but p95 high -> model perf. any other signals?

sam: add kv-cache-miss-rate and prefix-cache-hit to signals. model regressions often show increased decode time + more KV misses. capacity failure will show increased scheduling latency and infra errors (OOMs, preempt).

liam: UX: console should let SREs tune three knobs per rollout: breach_threshold (p95 ms), observation_window (seconds), recovery_strategy (regional|global|gradual). default: 350ms, 180s, regional.

maya: edge-case: what about A/B experiments with uneven reward metrics? if quality metric (like rerank score) improves but latency regresses slightly, auto swapback might hurt quality. need an allowlist where certain experiments opt out of auto-swapback or use multi-metric rules.

tara: yes — we need multi-metric guards. suggested API shape for rollout policy config in console: 
```
rollback_policy: {
  metrics: [ {name: "p95", op: ">", threshold: 350}, {name: "error_rate", op: ">", threshold: 0.01}],
  window_sec: 180,
  priority: ["regional", "variant", "global"],
  multi_metric_mode: "any" // or "all"
}
```

sam: one more: include a cooldown per-model so we don't flip-flop. e.g., once swapped back, block re-rollouts to the same variant for N minutes unless manually overridden.

liam: agree. cooldown default 30m. also emit a structured event for audit: rollout.swapback {reason, metrics_snapshot, action_taken} to our telemetry so product can build dashboards.

ops-bot: note: proposal recorded in /incidents/rollouts-runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollouts-auto-recovery

tara: ok plan: liam + maya to draft a minimal policy impl (regional-first, 3min window, cooldown 30m, multi-metric any by default). sam to add UX notes for console knobs and audit events. i'll open a PR for the runbook update. thanks :thumbsup:
